reason: Prioritize small active-loop changes that preserve FP32 update order and avoid extra packing. The 128-byte A slice matches the stated cache-line size, and the evidence does not show a conflict; 192-byte padding may alter set mapping, but it grows scratch from 64 KiB to 96 KiB while the panel’s B data is about 64 KiB, risking pressure on the 128 KiB L1D. Test it after lower-cost loop changes, and judge only the complete timed call. The prior padded-layout measurements changed the inactive full512 path and do not establish a result for this active panel32 proposal. Larger layout and transpose changes add substantial timed work and correctness risk.
